title: Adaptive Starter Allowance + SQ Trigger for Enterprise Conversion
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We will test an adaptive starter credit model designed to: 1) increase time-to-value for new developer signups, 2) surface high-value enterprise prospects earlier via a Security Questionnaire (SQ) trigger, and 3) reduce credit gaming while preserving PLG velocity. This ticket defines the hypothesis, experiment arms, instrumentation, rollout plan, risks, and acceptance criteria.

Hypothesis:
If we replace the one-size starter credit with adaptive, usage-aware allowances and an automated SQ trigger for accounts that cross enterprise thresholds, then we will increase paid conversion from free trials by ~15% at equivalent CAC while reducing churn from low-intent accounts.

Why now / Background:
Current starter credit is a flat grant with a 30-day expiry. We see two problems: (1) early heavy token consumption often wastes credits on low-value exploration, and (2) higher-intent enterprise prospects are not identified early enough for sales/solutions engagement; they often expire before SQ and contract conversations begin.

Experiment design - Arms:
- Control (C): Existing single grant of 10k credits, 30-day expiry.
- Variant A (V-A) - Vesting allowance: 3k immediate + 7k vesting daily over 30 days (auto-unlock). Designed to preserve runway for later evaluation and limit early credit dumping.
- Variant B (V-B) - Usage-contingent top-ups: initial 5k credits + algorithmic top-ups triggered on meaningful engagement signals (>=3 unique endpoints used OR >=5 chat sessions) up to 20k total, with two-step anti-abuse checks (captcha + email domain verification).
- Variant C (V-C) - SQ Trigger + Sales Signal: same as V-B but with an automated SQ invite + sales notification when usage OR spending rate exceeds enterprise threshold (>=100k tokens in 14 days OR sustained 7-day avg cost > $1/day).

Primary metrics:
- 30-day paid conversion rate (trial -> paid).
- Time-to-first-paid (days).
- Net new MRR attributable to experiment cohort at 90 days.
- SQ completion rate for triggered accounts (V-C).
- False positive rate for SQ trigger (accounts that hit threshold but have no enterprise intent).
- Credit utilization efficiency (paid conversions per token issued).

Secondary metrics / guardrails:
- Signups per day (to detect funnel drop).
- Abuse signals: bursty token patterns, single IP multi-account.
- Customer-reported friction (NPS/feedback).
- Support queue volume for SQ or account unlocks.

Instrumentation / dashboards:
- New cohort tags: experiment_arm (control, vesting, topup, sq-trigger).
- Events to record: credit_issue, credit_vest, credit_topup, sq_invite_sent, sq_completed, upgrade_success, support_request.
- Dashboards: trial-funnel by arm, SQ funnel (invite -> complete -> conversion), credit-efficiency heatmap.
- Tracking links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Adaptive+Starter+Allowance+PRD, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAdaptiveStarterAllowances, https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/402

Rollout plan:
1) Instrumentation and QA (2 weeks): events, cohort tagging, mock SQ flow, privacy/consent review.
2) Canary (10% new signups) for 1 week to validate instrumentation and abuse patterns.
3) A/B test split 25/25/25/25 across new signups for 4 weeks.
4) Evaluate metrics at 30d and 90d; if V-C drives statistically significant uplift in paid conversion and SQ completion with acceptable false positive rate and support load, promote as baseline for enterprise-track signups.

Dependencies:
- Billing team: support for algorithmic top-ups and new credit vesting APIs (ENG-52811).
- Console: sign-up flow UI to show vesting schedule and SQ invite modal (DES-33120).
- Security & Legal: review SQ automation and data collection for compliance.
- Support: playbook for unlocked accounts and SQ follow-ups.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Vesting may frustrate developers who expect bulk credits up front; mitigate with UX copy and an immediate demo template to show value early.
- SQ trigger could create false positives and generate support overhead; include progressive detection (usage + domain/reputation checks) and delay hard marketing until SQ completion.
- Top-ups introduce complexity in billing and abuse detection; require rate limits and heuristics.

Acceptance criteria / Success thresholds:
- Primary: >= 15% relative lift in 30-day paid conversion for V-C vs Control with p < 0.05 OR net positive ROI when factoring support and SD costs at 90 days.
- Secondary: SQ invite -> completion >= 25% for true-enterprise domains and false positive rate < 20%.
- No >10% drop in daily signups vs control.

Next steps / open questions:
- Fine-tune enterprise thresholds for SQ trigger (current proposal: 100k tokens in 14 days) — need historical cohort analysis.
- Decide maximum allowable top-up per account and friction points for verification.
- Confirm privacy wording and consent for automated SQ invites.
